page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, reaching clock frequencies up to 3.9 GHz. It includes hardware acceleration instructions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5, sustaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature dedicated hardware GPUs and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-threaded and integer capability. Single-core execution reflects higher efficiency, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 2189.0 and text processing benchmarks placing in the top decile. In compression tasks, single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression throughput also perform in the top 25 percentile. For machine learning, small model inference (135M parameters) yields text generation speeds of 388.45 tokens per second. Conversely, sustained multi-core benchmarks show middle-tier performance, with multi-core stress-ng at 17341.56, Geekbench multi-core at 13223.0, and static web serving throughput measuring 31.39 GB/sec.

The Flex tier utilizes a burstable CPU allocation design, offering a cost-efficient resource profile compared to fixed-allocation compute instances. This architecture trades sustained all-core saturation guarantees for lower running expenditure across standard 1:4 general-purpose operational profiles. The lack of bundled local NVMe drives and a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps represent key trade-offs to consider for I/O-intensive workloads.

The AWS m8i-flex.4xlarge is appropriately matched for general-purpose enterprise tasks that experience variable compute demand. Primary use cases include web serving fleets, enterprise application middleware, backend API hosting, build and CI/CD pipelines, and microservices requiring modern DDR5 memory throughput without persistent full-core CPU utilization.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.4xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable virtual instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz, complemented by 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory and 480 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs, utilizing network-attached storage and a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps. Benchmark metrics indicate strong single-core performance, particularly in data decompression, text processing, and lightweight LLM text generation, while overall multi-threaded throughput sits in the median range. Built for cost efficiency in variable workloads, it is suited for web serving, microservices, enterprise applications, and staging environments.
